\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ആസ്ത്മ} (āstma)}{ആസ്ത്മ (āstma)}]{\ml{ആസ്ത്മ} (āstma) — asthma}

\label{lesson:ML-C534-astma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to grow weak, then the Malayalam for breathlessness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ആസ്ത്മ}}
\textbf{\ml{ആസ്ത്മ}} — \emph{āstma} — \textquotedblleft{}asthma\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{തണുപ്പുകാലത്ത്} \ml{മുത്തശ്ശിക്ക്} \ml{ആസ്ത്മ} \ml{കൂടും}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taṇuppukālattŭ muttaśśikkŭ āstma kūṭuṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the cold season grandmother's asthma gets worse.
\end{quote}

A long-lasting illness; \ml{ശ്വാസംമുട്ട്} is the breathlessness it brings.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ആസ്ത്മ}} (\emph{āstma}) was borrowed from English \emph{asthma}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āstma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āstma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṇuppukālattŭ muttaśśikkŭ āstma kūṭuṁ.} — In the cold season grandmother's asthma gets worse.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to grow weak, then the Malayalam for breathlessness, then say \emph{āstma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ആസ്ത്മ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Asthma\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{നെഞ്ചെരിച്ചിൽ} (neñcericcil)}{നെഞ്ചെരിച്ചിൽ (neñcericcil)}]{\ml{നെഞ്ചെരിച്ചിൽ} (neñcericcil) — heartburn}

\label{lesson:ML-C534-nencericcil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for breathlessness, then the Malayalam for asthma.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{നെഞ്ചെരിച്ചിൽ}}
\textbf{\ml{നെഞ്ചെരിച്ചിൽ}} — \emph{neñcericcil} — \textquotedblleft{}heartburn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{എരിവുള്ള} \ml{ഭക്ഷണം} \ml{കഴിച്ചാൽ} \ml{എനിക്ക്} \ml{നെഞ്ചെരിച്ചിൽ} \ml{വരും}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{erivuḷḷa bhakṣaṇaṁ kaḻiccāl enikkŭ neñcericcil varuṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If I eat spicy food, I get heartburn.
\end{quote}

\ml{നെഞ്ച്} chest + \ml{എരിച്ചിൽ} burning, from \ml{എരിയുക}, to burn.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{നെഞ്ചെരിച്ചിൽ}} (\emph{neñcericcil}) is native Dravidian, a compound of \ml{നെഞ്ച്}, \textquotedblleft{}the chest\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3736), and \ml{എരിച്ചിൽ}, \textquotedblleft{}burning, smarting\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 811).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{neñcericcil}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{neñcericcil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{erivuḷḷa bhakṣaṇaṁ kaḻiccāl enikkŭ neñcericcil varuṁ.} — If I eat spicy food, I get heartburn.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for breathlessness, then the Malayalam for asthma, then say \emph{neñcericcil} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{നെഞ്ചെരിച്ചിൽ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Heartburn\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മലബന്ധം} (malabandhaṁ)}{മലബന്ധം (malabandhaṁ)}]{\ml{മലബന്ധം} (malabandhaṁ) — constipation}

\label{lesson:ML-C534-malabandham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for asthma, then the Malayalam for heartburn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മലബന്ധം}}
\textbf{\ml{മലബന്ധം}} — \emph{malabandhaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}constipation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വെള്ളം} \ml{കുറച്ച്} \ml{കുടിച്ചാൽ} \ml{മലബന്ധം} \ml{ഉണ്ടാകും}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{veḷḷaṁ kuṟaccŭ kuṭiccāl malabandhaṁ uṇṭākuṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Drinking too little water causes constipation.
\end{quote}

Literally a binding of the bowels: \ml{മലം}, waste, is its first part. A word of the doctor's room.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മലബന്ധം}} (\emph{malabandhaṁ}) is a learned compound built from Sanskrit \emph{mala}, \textquotedblleft{}dirt, excretion\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9899), and \emph{bandha}, \textquotedblleft{}a bond, a damming\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9136).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malabandhaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malabandhaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{veḷḷaṁ kuṟaccŭ kuṭiccāl malabandhaṁ uṇṭākuṁ.} — Drinking too little water causes constipation.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for asthma, then the Malayalam for heartburn, then say \emph{malabandhaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മലബന്ധം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Constipation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഉറക്കമില്ലായ്മ} (uṟakkamillāyma)}{ഉറക്കമില്ലായ്മ (uṟakkamillāyma)}]{\ml{ഉറക്കമില്ലായ്മ} (uṟakkamillāyma) — insomnia; sleeplessness}

\label{lesson:ML-C534-urakkamillayma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for heartburn, then the Malayalam for constipation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഉറക്കമില്ലായ്മ}}
\textbf{\ml{ഉറക്കമില്ലായ്മ}} — \emph{uṟakkamillāyma} — \textquotedblleft{}insomnia; sleeplessness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പരീക്ഷക്കാലത്ത്} \ml{അവന്} \ml{ഉറക്കമില്ലായ്മ} \ml{ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{parīkṣakkālattŭ avanŭ uṟakkamillāyma uṇṭāyirunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He suffered from sleeplessness during the exams.
\end{quote}

\ml{ഉറക്കം} sleep + \ml{ഇല്ലായ്മ} a lack: -\ml{ഇല്ലായ്മ} turns \ml{ഇല്ല} into a noun of lacking.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഉറക്കമില്ലായ്മ}} (\emph{uṟakkamillāyma}) is native Dravidian, a compound of \ml{ഉറക്കം}, \textquotedblleft{}sleep\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 707), and \ml{ഇല്ലായ്മ}, \textquotedblleft{}not being\textquotedblright{}, from \ml{ഇല്ല} (DEDR 2559).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṟakkamillāyma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṟakkamillāyma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parīkṣakkālattŭ avanŭ uṟakkamillāyma uṇṭāyirunnu.} — He suffered from sleeplessness during the exams.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for heartburn, then the Malayalam for constipation, then say \emph{uṟakkamillāyma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഉറക്കമില്ലായ്മ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Insomnia; sleeplessness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ചുമയ്ക്കുക} (cumaykkuka)}{ചുമയ്ക്കുക (cumaykkuka)}]{\ml{ചുമയ്ക്കുക} (cumaykkuka) — to have a cough; to cough}

\label{lesson:ML-C534-cumaykkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for constipation, then the Malayalam for insomnia.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ചുമയ്ക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ചുമയ്ക്കുക}} — \emph{cumaykkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to have a cough; to cough\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{രാത്രി} \ml{മുഴുവൻ} \ml{കുട്ടി} \ml{ചുമച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rātri muḻuvan kuṭṭi cumaccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child coughed all night.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ചുമച്ചു}, \emph{cumaccu}.

The noun \ml{ചുമ}, a cough, is already familiar. The past is \ml{ചുമച്ചു}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ചുമയ്ക്കുക}} (\emph{cumaykkuka}) is native Dravidian, the verb beside \ml{ചുമ}, \textquotedblleft{}a cough\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1964).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cumaykkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cumaykkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rātri muḻuvan kuṭṭi cumaccu.} — The child coughed all night.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for constipation, then the Malayalam for insomnia, then say \emph{cumaykkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ചുമയ്ക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To have a cough; to cough\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
